brief.headline: Memory cycle intact: HBM supply sold through 2H26, DRAM/NAND pricing +58-75% QoQ in Q2; Samsung/SK capex spree signals no discipline concerns yet
brief.summary: <cite index="11-2,11-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following Q1's record 93-98% surge, while NAND Flash prices jumped 70-75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="4-4,4-20">Top three memory makers have allocated full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2</cite>. <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%</cite>. <cite index="36-11,36-12">SK Hynix announced 100 trillion KRW ($64B) investment including M17 NAND fab operational by 1H 2029 and 20 trillion won for P&T7 advanced packaging expansion</cite>. <cite index="19-2,19-6">Hyperscaler AI capex climbed from $400B in 2025 to likely close to $700B in 2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-long SK Hynix vs Samsung. SK holds structural HBM lead (57% share vs Samsung 22% in Q4'25) and locked Nvidia Rubin allocation. Samsung playing catch-up on HBM3E qual but capex announcement (800 trillion won joint commitment) shows no profitability panic. Near-term volatility (both names down 7-9% on Jul 2 global tech selloff) creates entry but pair spread tight—no clear alpha until Samsung HBM4 ramp visibility or SK packaging bottleneck emerges. Watch for Samsung HBM3E Nvidia qualification update and SK's M17 NAND timeline vs enterprise SSD tightness.

memory_cycle.notes: Q2 2026 pricing still +58-75% QoQ but down from Q1's +90-95% record surge. HBM allocation sold through 2026, wafer capacity structurally reallocated from commodity to HBM (3:1 conversion ratio). Consumer demand destruction real (smartphone -14% 2026E, PC -13.6%) but AI server/enterprise SSD demand absorbing all incremental supply. TrendForce projects Q3 gains moderate to +13-18% DRAM, +10-15% NAND as high base effects hit. No meaningful new capacity until late 2027-2028. Cycle risk: hyperscaler capex-to-revenue gap widening ($600B annual per Sequoia), but arms-race dynamics prevent unilateral cuts.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-16">SK Hynix emerged as primary beneficiary, only supplier delivering both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale</cite>. <cite index="9-8">HBM4 commands ~40% price premium over HBM3E even after absorbing 50% higher cost-per-bit</cite>. <cite index="34-5">Nvidia secured ~60% of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS capacity (130K wpm by year-end)</cite>. <cite index="28-1,28-2">TSMC CoWoS capacity projected 120-130K wpm by end-2026, up from 13K at end-2023, driven by B200/GB200 and MI300X/MI400 demand</cite>. Samsung struggling on HBM3E qual but <cite index="40-6">in 'close discussion' to supply HBM4 to Nvidia</cite>. <cite index="4-12">HBM3E consumes ~3x wafer area of standard DDR5 due to larger dies and stacking yield losses</cite>. Watch: Samsung HBM qualification progress, SK Hynix HBM4 ramp linearity, CoWoS supply allocation shifts.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion KRW investment: M17 NAND fab by 2029, P&T7 packaging expansion
news_pulse.implication: NAND capacity relief timeline pushes to 2029; near-term enterprise SSD shortage persists. P&T7 packaging targets HBM/DRAM assembly bottleneck. Capex discipline intact—no panic expansion despite record margins.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix pledge 800 trillion won ($518B) for four new mega-fabs in SW Korea; gov targets 2x DRAM capacity in 5 years
news_pulse.implication: Government-orchestrated cluster (no tech collaboration). Signals long-term conviction but relief timeline 2028-2029. Implies current pricing power sustainable multi-year. Risk: overbuilding if AI capex decelerates post-2027.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ Q2 2026, NAND +70-75%; Q1 saw record +93-98% DRAM surge
news_pulse.implication: Deceleration from Q1 parabola but still extreme gains. NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle (enterprise SSD tightness). Q3 guidance +13-18% DRAM, +10-15% NAND—moderation continues but pricing power intact through 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Top three memory makers allocated full HBM output for 2026; Micron Q2 gross margin 68%
news_pulse.implication: HBM allocation wall through 2026 confirmed. 68% GM (Micron) vs ~40% historical underscores pricing power. Implies Samsung/SK Hynix HBM profitability windfall. Consumer DRAM/NAND deprioritized—cost pass-through to PC/smartphone OEMs.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance $690B, up 81% YoY; Goldman sees $5.3T cumulative 2025-2030
news_pulse.implication: Demand ceiling remains invisible. 75% of capex direct AI infrastructure (GPUs, HBM servers, networking). Arms-race dynamics prevent unilateral cuts. Risk: widening capex-to-revenue gap ($600B annually per Sequoia) pressures ROI narrative, but no evidence of budget fatigue yet.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to hit 120-130K wpm by end-2026, 10x vs end-2023; Nvidia locked ~60% allocation
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing but Nvidia dominance (60% allocation) squeezes AMD/Broadcom/hyperscaler custom silicon. Samsung/SK Hynix HBM output gated by TSMC packaging unless in-house (SK P&T7) or OSATs (ASE/Amkor) scale. CoPoS (panel-level) pilot live, mass production 2028+.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix shares plunge 7-9% Jul 2 on Nasdaq selloff; SK closed -14.6%, Samsung -9.1%
news_pulse.implication: Risk-off deleveraging, not fundamental deterioration. YTD gains (Samsung +114%, SK +186% through May) left names crowded. Entry opportunity if hyperscaler capex guidance holds. Watch for positioning unwind vs structural HBM/DRAM demand decoupling.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q4 2025 HBM revenue share 57% vs Samsung 22%, Micron 21%; SK expects HBM demand > supply through 2028
news_pulse.implication: SK structural lead on HBM validated. Samsung clawing back from qual issues but still 2.5x share gap. Micron gaining but capacity constrained. SK pricing power on HBM4 (40% premium) into Nvidia Rubin 2027 ramp. Risk: Samsung HBM3E/4 qual success narrows gap faster than expected.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KOSPI options data in payload; ADR flow (SSNLF, HXSCL OTC) illiquid. Jul 2 selloff (-7-9%) likely triggered stop-loss cascades and delta-hedging. If ADR vol spikes into US session, suggests institutional unwind vs retail capitulation. Watch KOSPI 200 futures for overnight gap risk and Samsung/SK single-stock option skew (if available via KRX) for directional conviction post-capex announcement. Elevated vol = pairs opportunity; subdued vol = conviction waning.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung Electronics HBM3E Nvidia qualification update or HBM4 supply agreement leak
Micron/SK Hynix commentary on Q3 DRAM/NAND contract pricing negotiations (TrendForce already guiding deceleration to +13-18% DRAM, +10-15% NAND)
Hyperscaler (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META) capex guidance reaffirmation or pullback chatter into mid-July earnings
TSMC CoWoS allocation rumors (AMD MI400, Broadcom custom AI, hyperscaler silicon vs Nvidia Rubin priority)
KOSPI rebound sustainability—watch energy/construction/power sectors (AI infrastructure beneficiaries) vs memory stock divergence
